Under batched conditions , throughput scales toward the processor's fused multiply-accumulate peak

of quantized large language models . The architecture centers around memory-bandwidth saturation during token decoding and compute saturation during prompt prefill and batched execution . Modern CPUs possess sophisticated memory hierarchies with multiple levels of cache , including high-speed L1 data caches , larger unified or per-core L2 caches , and massive shared L3 caches spanning tens or hundreds of megabytes . However , model parameter sizes for practical language models typically exceed several gigabytes , far outstripping the cache capacities of contemporary processors . Consequently , single-user autoregressive decoding is inherently bound by the bandwidth of the main memory interface . In each autoregressive generation step
step , the model must read all weight matrices corresponding to the active layers from memory into the processor registers to perform matrix-vector multiplication against the hidden state vector . For a model with several billion parameters stored in quantized formats such as Q4 K M , Q8 0 , or ternary representations like PQ2 0 , every token generated demands moving megabytes or gigabytes across the memory bus . If a machine sustains forty gigabytes per second of memory bandwidth and the active weights occupy two gigabytes , the absolute theoretical upper bound on generation speed is twenty tokens per second , regardless of compute capabilities . To reach and sustain this memory ceiling , an inference engine must eliminate all extraneous memory traffic , optimize memory access patterns for CPU streaming hardware , minimize synchronization overhead among worker threads , and ensure instruction sequences achieve optimal retirement rates without pipeline stalls . In each autoregressive generation step , the model must read all weight matrices corresponding to the active layers from memory into the processor registers to perform matrix-vector multiplication against the hidden state vector . If a machine sustains forty gigabytes per second of memory bandwidth and the active weights occupy two gigabytes , the absolute theoretical upper bound on generation speed is twenty tokens per second , regardless of compute capabilities . To reach and sustain this memory ceiling , an inference engine must eliminate all extraneous memory traffic , optimize memory access patterns for C
larger unified or per-core L2 caches , and massive shared L3 caches spanning tens or hundreds of megabytes . However , model parameter sizes for practical language models typically exceed several gigabytes , far outstripping the cache capacities of contemporary processors . Consequently , single-user autoregressive decoding is inherently bound by the bandwidth of the main memory interface . However , model parameter sizes for practical language models typically exceed several gigabytes , far outstripping the cache capacities of contemporary processors . Consequently , single-user autoregressive decoding is inherently bound by the bandwidth of the main memory interface . In each autoregressive generation step , the model must read all weight matrices corresponding to the active layers from memory into the processor registers to perform matrix-vector multiplication against the hidden state vector . For a model with several billion parameters stored in quantized formats such as Q4 K M , Q8 0 , or ternary representations like PQ2 0 , every token generated demands moving megabytes or gigabytes across the memory bus . If a machine sustains forty gigabytes per second of memory bandwidth and the active weights occupy two gigabytes , the absolute theoretical upper bound on generation speed is twenty tokens per second , regardless of compute capabilities . To reach and sustain this memory ceiling , an inference engine must eliminate all extraneous memory traffic , optimize memory access patterns for CPU streaming hardware , minimize synchronization overhead among worker threads , and ensure instruction sequences achieve optimal retirement rates without pipeline stalls . When serving multiple concurrent users , the computational characteristics shift . By batching concurrent requests together , the engine can amortize the cost of reading weights across multiple user tokens , transforming memory-bound matrix-vector products into compute-intensive matrix-matrix multiplications . Under batched conditions , throughput scales toward the processor's fused multiply-accumulate peak , bounded by vector unit widths and core counts . Benchmarking language model engines requires rigorous methodology . A single measurement taken in isolation is susceptible to operating system background tasks , dynamic frequency scaling fluctuations , thermal throttling , and memory subsystem contention . Accurate performance characterization demands repeated , interleaved executions across reference and competing

To reach and sustain this memory ceiling , an inference engine must eliminate all extraneous memory traffic , optimize memory access patterns for CPU streaming hardware , minimize synchronization overhead among worker threads , and ensure instruction sequences achieve optimal retirement rates without pipeline stalls . When serving multiple concurrent users , the computational characteristics shift . By batching concurrent requests together , the engine can amortize the cost of reading weights across multiple user tokens , transforming memory-bound matrix-vector products into compute-intensive matrix-matrix multiplications . Under batched conditions , throughput scales toward the processor's fused multiply-accumulate peak , bounded by vector unit widths and core counts . Benchmarking language model engines requires rigorous methodology . A single measurement taken in isolation is susceptible to operating system background tasks , dynamic frequency scaling fluctuations , thermal throttling , and memory subsystem contention . Accurate performance characterization demands repeated , interleaved executions across reference and competing engines under identical hardware and software conditions . Reporting medians alongside statistical spreads ensures that transient noise is identified and discounted , while comparing achieved performance against theoretical and measured hardware ceilings provides an objective metric of architectural efficiency . The Peregrine inference engine is designed for high-performance CPU execution of quantized large language models . The architecture centers around memory-bandwidth saturation during token decoding and compute saturation during prompt prefill and batched execution . When serving multiple concurrent users , the computational characteristics shift . By batching concurrent requests together , the engine can amortize the cost of reading weights across multiple user tokens , transforming memory-bound matrix-vector products into compute-intensive matrix-matrix multiplications . Under batched conditions , throughput scales toward the processor's fused multiply-accumulate peak , bounded by vector unit widths and core counts . Benchmarking language model engines requires rigorous methodology . A single measurement taken in isolation is susceptible to operating system background tasks , dynamic frequency scaling fluctuations , thermal throttling , and memory subsystem contention . Accurate performance characterization demands repeated , interleaved executions across reference and competing engines under identical hardware and software conditions . Reporting medians alongside statistical spreads ensures that transient noise is identified and discounted , while comparing achieved performance against theoretical and measured hardware ceilings provides an objective metric of architectural efficiency . The Peregrine inference engine is designed for high-performance CPU execution of quantized large language models . The architecture centers around memory-bandwidth saturation during token decoding and compute saturation during prompt prefill and batched execution . Modern CPUs possess sophisticated memory hierarchies with multiple levels of cache , including high-speed L1 data caches , larger unified or per-core L2 caches , and massive shared L3 caches spanning tens or hundreds of megabytes . However , model parameter sizes for practical language models typically exceed several gigabytes , far outstripping the cache capacities of contemporary processors .
